summary: Children are guaranteed a share of the estate that a will cannot remove. Iceland has no trust law and is outside the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations exist as self-owned institutions.
reserved_share: Descendants are forced heirs under Inheritance Act 8/1962; a secondary source gives half of the intestate share. The article and fraction were not confirmed in the statute.
foreign_law_note: Nordic conflict rules apply the law of the deceased's domicile; whether a foreigner may choose their national law was not confirmed.
trust_note: No trust law. Self-owned institutions under Act 33/1999 can serve as foundations, but family benefit is restricted.
open_questions: Forced share fraction in Act 8/1962 (a secondary source conflicts with arithmetic from intestacy rules).
Whether a family foundation is allowed.
